segments.text: Hey friends, do you know what F**k You money means?
Now look, I’m not using any random abusive word here.
F**k You money — also called FU money — is actually a mindset.
And to understand it, I want to give you an example. You’ll have to imagine
this example, and I literally want you to close your eyes and imagine.
Imagine this — a big business owner is standing in front of you.
He wants to work with you and has come to meet you.
He’s holding a cheque in his hand.
The amount written on that cheque is 10 crores.
He’s ready to give you that 10 crore cheque.
The guy is completely genuine —
a businessman — and the deal is such that you have to work for
him for one week. Now the work he’s offering is also in your field.
You can do it.
It won’t be too much of a problem.
But still, if at that point you say **no** to him — why? Maybe you don’t like
the businessman’s character? Maybe you’re not in the mood to work that day?
Or maybe you just want to spend more time with your family? Whatever the reason
may be — the main point is: **imagine that.** If you’ve reached a
point where you can say **no** to even a
huge amount of money — you can say **F
U** — and not because of ego, but because you’ve already achieved ultimate
financial freedom.
You’re still working, but you’re not dependent on money anymore.
You have no stress about paying bills.
No tension about loan EMIs. You can do whatever work you want, as much as you
want, whenever you want. You can choose the people you want
to work with. And you can do all this from any corner of the world.
It means you’ve reached that level of freedom. Just
imagine — if your life actually becomes like this, wouldn’t it feel amazing?
Of course it would, right?
Total bliss. And this mindset, this exact
thing is called **achieving FU money status** — where you’re
no longer dependent on money. Just imagine, if this kind of life becomes
your reality — how would it feel? And if your mind is telling you, “Come
on, this doesn’t really happen,” then I’ll genuinely ask you this — Haven’t
you ever heard even one story of a person who has achieved that level of wealth?
Someone who doesn’t
even need to think about money anymore? What I’m going to talk about today
is directly related to this topic — How you can create that kind of mindset for
yourself. How you can achieve a life where you can truly say **FU money**.
The book I’m going to talk about today is written by an author who has already
achieved that status — and he himself will tell you how he did it, and how
**you** can reach that level
too. But before that, once again, I want you to imagine — close your eyes
if you want — a lavish life where you have everything you once dreamed of.
You have an amazing car.
You’re eating lavish meals.
You’re wearing branded clothes. Basically, everything you ever
wanted in life — you now have it. Now, I want you to shift a little
from imagination to **reality**. And in fact, even the author says the same
— that once you come back to reality, you should **literally start writing**.
If you want to live a lavish and extraordinary life — if you truly want
that kind of lifestyle — then how much would it cost you?
Start writing it down freely, without holding back your heart or mind. How much
would you spend on food? If you buy the clothes you want, how much would that
cost? Make a rough estimate — and then start defining it clearly, in detail.
That author did something very similar too — and eventually arrived at a
**final amount**. That final amount becomes your **destination**
— the point you need to reach. I want you to do the same.
Whatever your final amount comes out to be, break it down in detail.
The more detailed you go, the better clarity
you’ll get. You’ll clearly understand how much it would actually cost to live a
good, lavish life. So, calculate how much your expenses would
be **per year**, and then write that amount in the comments. Now watch...
As I told you, **this** is your target — this is your **destination** where
you need to reach. And to reach this destination, you now have two vehicles.
These are the two vehicles that most people use to achieve their dream, lavish
life. The **first vehicle** moves slowly — very slowly. And the thing is,
**you won’t be the one driving this slow vehicle — someone else will drive it.**
But the vehicle will keep moving slowly, steadily.
For sure — if you stay disciplined and keep sitting in it, one day it **will**
take you to your destination. Now, the problem
with this vehicle is that it’s **slow**. And by “slow vehicle,” I mean **saving
and investing** — in mutual funds, SIPs — and then **patiently waiting over time**.
One day, your wealth will compound, and you’ll achieve your dream. The good
thing about this vehicle is that it’s **very safe**, and it gives
you **certainty** — all
it needs is discipline. But the downside is — **it’s slow**.
On the other hand, you also have a **second option** — the **fast vehicle**.
Now, with this fast vehicle, the catch is — **there’s no driver for it**.
You’ll have to drive that vehicle **yourself**.
The good thing is — you’ll have **more control** over it. Yes, you’ll need
to put in more **effort**, but if you’re willing to work hard, ready
to learn and understand how the road ahead will be, then this vehicle can
take you to your destination **faster**. Now, my question to you is: **Would
you like to sit in Vehicle A — the slow one, or Vehicle B — the fast one?**
If you’ve chosen **Vehicle A**, then this video isn’t for you. I
have another video on investments — go watch that one instead.
But if you’re interested in driving **Vehicle B** — the one the author himself
drove, and to some extent, even I have driven — if you want to learn this path
and want to become wealthy **comparatively faster** (I’m not
saying *fast*, just *faster than usual*), then this video is for you.
So now I’m going to share a story with you. There are many lessons hidden
in that story. I want you to **listen carefully** and later tell me — how many
wrong mindsets, bad habits, or false rules the person in the story is following.
After finishing the story, I’ll
tell you the correct answers and explain everything.
What are the wrong rules? But first, listen to the story. There was a man
named **Vikram**, around 30 years old. He lived in a small rented house, and like
every other night, he couldn’t sleep tonight either. He was staring
at the peeling paint on the wall, thinking — when will his luck shine? When will
he live in a big, luxurious house of his own? When will he become rich?
Now, it’s not like he wasn’t doing anything to achieve that dream. Since
childhood, he had learned one thing from his parents: **“Son, if you want
to become rich, don’t waste money — save it.”** He had taken this lesson
deeply to heart and truly believed
in it. That’s why, every single day, he focused on **saving money**.
He ate the cheapest food possible and lived in a small rented house that was far
from his office — but since it was cheap, he chose it anyway. He always bought
second-hand things, and he was living such a struggle-filled life that
even his friends would often tell him, “Bro, you should buy
some new things.” But he would reply, **”New things don’t bring happiness.
Money doesn’t bring happiness.”**
“I’m happy like this,” he would say — even though it wasn’t true. Whenever his
friends told him good things about rich people, he would get irritated and say,
**“All these people move ahead by doing shady or dishonest work. Rich people are
either just plain lucky, or their fathers and grandfathers left them a lot
of money.”** “They’re able to do all that because they have it easy. But people
like us — if we want to become rich, we have to work really hard. We’ll have
to hustle day and night, and only then, slowly, over time, we might become rich.”
“But it’s okay,” he’d say, “I still have a lot of time. One day, I’ll also start
a business and become rich.” And when
his friends would ask him, **“Then why haven’t you started your business yet?”**
He says, “No, the right time hasn’t come yet.
First I need to improve my communication skills.
I have to learn video editing so that when I launch my business, I can
make videos to market it.” With three or four reasons like that, he explains why
he isn’t starting now—but insists he definitely will start
one day. Now my question to you is: **Do you think this makes sense?**
Will this Vikram become rich anytime soon? Now, if you ask the author of the
**FU Money** book — the answer is **absolutely not**. Because
Vikram hasn’t just
adopted one or two, but **eight** wrong habits in his mindset. And because
of these, he’ll **never** become rich. So what are those 8 habits?
Let’s look at them — and see if **you** can relate to or understand them too.
The **first** one is: **“Money can’t buy happiness.”** Now look, in life…
Whatever we do in life — whether it’s staying healthy, traveling, buying a car,
or owning a house — we do all of it for **happiness**, to feel happy.
But on the other hand, you must have often heard this too: **“Money can’t buy
happiness.”** Now,
if you keep thoughts like that in your mind — if somewhere deep inside,
this formula is wired into your brain that **money and happiness can’t coexist** —
Now tell me — will you really feel like earning money with that mindset?
**Obviously not.** Yes, it’s true — **money can’t
buy happiness**. **But neither can being poor.** You can’t buy happiness by being
poor either. **Happiness is a state of mind** — a perspective, a way of looking
at the world and choosing to stay happy, which you can definitely practice. But
on the other hand, also think about this: **Money gives you powerful leverage
to access happiness.**
For example, if traveling
brings you happiness — but because you’re so busy chasing money in your job and
daily life, you don’t get the time for it — then when you have money, you can
**hire someone**, **buy back your time**. You can then use that time —
in exchange for money — to do the things that **genuinely bring you happiness**.
The next wrong mindset is: **“Rich people are a**holes.”\*\* You must have heard
people say things like: “These rich people are terrible.” “They
do shady business.” “That
guy got ahead in life by doing all kinds of unethical stuff.” And you
may have noticed — **rich people often get a lot of hate.** If a
rich person does something wrong,
it becomes a huge issue — everyone makes a big deal out of it.
Now look, I’m not here to defend rich people.
That’s not what I’m doing. I’m saying this so you understand one thing clearly
— **Think of it like a formula in your mind:** **Rich people =
A**holes\*\* If that belief gets hardwired
in your brain — that rich people are bad — then here’s my question for you:
**Would you ever want to become an a**hole?\*\* Of course not. But
if your mind has linked **a**hole = rich\*\*, then
deep down, **you’ll never allow yourself to become rich**.
That’s why you need to **remove this mental blockage**
too. Don’t feel **envy** toward rich people — feel **inspired** by them.
You don’t need to follow the bad things they do — **but you should definitely
learn from the good things they do.** And always remember this: **You can
be rich and still be a happy, good person.**
There are **good poor people**, and **bad poor people** — just like there are
**good rich people**, and **bad
rich people**. **Goodness or badness has nothing to do with money.**
The next mindset — which even **Vikram** had — is: **“We have time.”** I had
made a video a while ago — if you haven’t seen it, do check it out — in that
video, I specifically calculated
and explained how we **barely** have enough time to work on our dreams. The
actual time we have for ourselves is **very, very limited**. What you see
on the screen
— do you really think that much time is enough to fulfill your dreams?
If you feel that the time is **less**, then what exactly
are you waiting for? You need to **start working right
now**. And I’m not saying you need to hustle round the clock — you can work
at your own pace, calmly. But one thing you absolutely
need to remove from your mind is this thought:
**“There’s still a lot of time to become rich.”**
You’ll have to **start from today itself**.
If you begin working on your skills today — especially **business skills**
— it will take time to build them. Only **after that** will you start making
more money. So don’t wait for old age. **Start now.** Next wrong mindset:
**“You have to be lucky.”** I’ve heard this too — people saying, **“Rich
people are just lucky.
It’s all luck.”** ...that’s the **reason** they move ahead
in life. But here’s my question: **Bill Gates,
Mark Zuckerberg**, or anyone else you consider rich or powerful — if all their
wealth was taken away, if their name and fame were taken away
too — do you think they’d still be able to build a business again? Well, let
me tell you the truth — there’s a **very high chance** that these people **would
absolutely build a business again.**
Yes, maybe they won’t reach the **billion-dollar** mark again — but
they’ll definitely become **millionaires**. Why? Because they’ve
gained so much **experience and learning**.
Sure, luck played a role — I agree. **But you can actually increase your own “luck
factor” too.** I had made a video on this as well — it was a summary of the
book **“The Luck Factor,”** where I
explained how, by working on your **mindset** and
your **actions**, you can actually **increase your own luck**.
If you’re interested in watching that summary, I’ll add
the link in the **i-button** and in the **description** — you can check
it out from there. Next wrong mindset: **“You have to be a cheapskate.”**
Again, I’ve seen many people — and I’m sure you have too — who are extremely
focused on earning money, but then they start
cutting corners everywhere, thinking: “How can I save money here?” “How can I
avoid spending there?” They become so obsessed with **saving money**
that many times, it actually ends up **costing them much more**.
For example, let’s take Vikram. This guy chose a house that was one and a half
to two hours away from his office — just to **save some money** on rent. But what
he didn’t realize was that **he was wasting 3–4 hours every single day** just
in commuting. In those 3–4 hours, if he wanted, he could’ve used his
**existing skills** to do some freelancing and
earn extra money, or even learned a **new skill** to increase his income.
The money he could’ve earned would have been **much more than the rent** he was
trying to save — which, by the way, he still had
to pay. But this difference in thinking is called
the **scarcity vs abundance mindset**. If you truly want
to become rich in life, then you **have to break free
from the scarcity mindset**. There’s **plenty of money out there**, and **you
too can earn a lot of it**. Ingrain this thinking into yourself. **Next:**
“You must get rich slow” — This is another common pattern that forms
in the mind, that **if you want to become rich, it can only happen slowly**.
It’s absolutely true that you **shouldn’t run after quick money**
or **get-rich-quick schemes** — those are often scams. But you must also
remember that **becoming rich doesn’t necessarily have to take a very long
time** either. If you work hard with full dedication and consistency, there
are **many entrepreneurs who have become rich quickly** — and **you can too**.
At the very least, you must **hold on to this belief** within yourself
— your aim should be to focus on the **speed of action**. Next: “You have
to work hard.” Many people say that to become rich, you need to work really
hard — **only** if you work very hard will you become
rich. But notice this: **Rich people don’t become wealthy just because
of hard work**. They become rich **because of smart work**.
They understand and **use the power of leverage**.
Instead of doing all the hard work themselves, **they
hire someone else by paying a little
money**. Just notice this yourself — on one side, there are
10 people, and on the other side, it’s just you alone. Let’s say **you
can work 5 hours a day** on a project. These
10 people can also work 5 hours each on the same project. So where you alone
would be able to put in **just 5 hours a
day**, **they can contribute 50 hours in a single day**.
These people end up working a total of 50 hours — and 50 hours is **10 times
more** than what you can do alone. So you too can **leverage** this kind
of system. **Smart people take advantage of leverage
like this.** They don’t just work hard — they work smart. Their aim is
to get **maximum
output with minimum effort**, and that should be your goal too. Next: **”You
must be perfectly ready.”** This is one example I see **almost every day**.
Many times, I’ve seen so many people who say, “I want to get into content creation.
I want to make videos.” So I ask them, “Why aren’t you starting then?” And they
say, “Bro, because I don’t even know which camera
to buy, which mic to use, which lights to get.
I don’t have a studio yet — I’ll
build a studio first.” Only after that, they say they’ll start making videos.
“I’ll buy this first, then I’ll start.” Basically,
people think they’ll only start once everything is perfect — and then they’ll
get results. Or deep down, there’s a fear of failure, a fear of being judged.
That’s why they hide behind these excuses like,
“I’ll start soon, I’ll make videos.” What will people
say? Many times, people don’t admit it, but deep down, they are scared.
There’s a fear of being perfect — a fear of appearing perfect so that people don’t
judge you. But the truth is, this mindset will never make you rich, let alone rich
quickly. You never need to be perfectly ready. You have to take action first
and then improve gradually. Again, just like it’s explained
in *The Lean Startup* — create a minimum viable product.
The biggest mistake most startup owners make is that they try to build a perfect
product, investing lakhs
of rupees and spending several years on it. Then, when they finally
launch the product in the market, people don’t buy it. True smartness lies
in this — if they had first created a minimum viable product,
something basic that could at least solve a small problem for a few people...
Then they launched it, took feedback from customers about what needed to change
and what didn’t, and made those changes based on the feedback before giving
it back to the customers. When this cycle keeps repeating, that’s how
big businesses are built.
That’s how good ideas turn into great ones. So again, how does
all this happen? By not waiting for everything to be perfect before starting
— and this mindset is something you should avoid holding onto as well.
These were the eight mindsets, eight habits, and eight rules that you
absolutely must follow if you don’t want to remain poor. This book also shares
many more strategic insights on how you can achieve FU Money status.

insights from such books, make sure to subscribe to the channel. In the
